findings.title: Dense, Unprotected Stage Counter Can Be Faulted to Skip S-Box Computation
findings.location: aes_sbox_dom: count_q/count_d, out_req_o, and we assignments
findings.description: The five-cycle security-critical sequencing is controlled by an ordinary 3-bit binary counter with no redundant encoding, sequence validation, or error indication. A single-bit fault can change count_q from 3'b000 directly to 3'b100, causing out_req_o to assert before any stage register is updated. Other single-bit transitions, such as 3'b001 to 3'b011, skip an internal inversion stage. Values 5 through 7 are also accepted as normal counter values and eventually wrap back to zero without raising an alert. Consequently, a clock, voltage, EM, or localized register fault can cause stale or partially computed masked outputs to be accepted as a completed S-Box result. When AES outputs are observable, repeatable stage-skipping faults can corrupt encryption or decryption and provide a differential-fault-analysis path to key recovery. The module exposes no error output through which the enclosing AES block could distinguish this condition from a valid completion.
findings.recommendation: Replace the binary counter with a hardened sparse-encoded FSM or redundant counters that validate the exact 0-to-4 stage sequence. Treat every invalid state, unexpected transition, or disagreement as a terminal error: suppress out_req_o, disable all stage write enables, clear sensitive intermediate registers, and propagate a fatal alert to the AES control block. Completion should only be generated after independently confirming that every required stage executed exactly once.

findings.title: Legal PipelineMul Configuration Disables Required First-Order Leakage Protection
findings.location: aes_sbox_dom parameter PipelineMul and gen_no_pipeline paths in aes_dom_indep_mul_gf2pn and aes_dom_dep_mul_gf2pn
findings.description: PipelineMul is a public synthesis parameter whose legal value 1'b0 selects unpipelined multiplier implementations. The selected branches explicitly integrate newly arriving inner-domain inputs with reshared or blinded cross-domain values retained from the previous evaluation. The source comments acknowledge that these transitions can cause SCA leakage. Because aes_sbox_dom is marked as implementing KEY.MASKING but contains no elaboration-time prohibition or security-status indication for this configuration, an integration can synthesize a functionally correct AES S-Box that does not preserve the claimed first-order DOM security at transaction boundaries. An attacker able to request repeated AES operations and measure power or EM emissions can exploit these old/new-value transitions to recover information correlated with sensitive AES state.
findings.recommendation: For production configurations claiming first-order masking, require PipelineMul == 1'b1 with an elaboration-time assertion or remove the insecure parameterization from aes_sbox_dom. If the unpipelined option must remain supported, add the registers needed to align all inner-domain, cross-domain, and blinded terms across transaction boundaries, then re-run glitch-aware probing-security verification on that exact synthesized configuration and synthesis-cell mapping.
